articles.title: Agentic AI: User Empowerment or Enclosure?
articles.summary: The paper argues that whether agentic AI empowers users will depend less on model capability alone and more on governance choices embedded in APIs, protocols, standards, and default configurations. Drawing comparisons to ad blockers, recommender systems, robo-advisors, and spam governance, it warns that agentic AI infrastructure could either preserve user-aligned agency or enclose it within proprietary systems.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is not a direct investable company update, but it highlights an important adoption issue: control over agentic AI workflows may be shaped by emerging protocols and industry governance before users or regulators fully engage. For advisors, the read-through is that platform architecture and standards could become key determinants of competitive advantage, regulatory scrutiny, and long-term monetization in agentic AI ecosystems.

articles.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
articles.summary: OpenForgeRL is an open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end inside the same inference harnesses and environments where they are deployed. It uses a lightweight proxy and Kubernetes-based rollout orchestration to connect complex multi-turn, tool-using agent workflows with standard reinforcement learning systems, improving benchmark performance for claw-based and GUI/browser-use agents while highlighting remaining weaknesses such as error recovery.
articles.advisor_relevance: This points to continued progress in making AI agents more reliable in real-world, multi-step workflows involving tools, browsers, and external systems. While still research-oriented, the framework highlights the growing importance of orchestration layers, scalable containerized infrastructure, and reinforcement learning techniques that could support future enterprise agent adoption.
